newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to pay 23 bln marks for Eurofighter force.
newsitem.headline: Germany to pay 23 bln marks for Eurofighter force.

text.p: The German defence ministry said on Friday it would pay a total of 23 billion marks ($14.3 billion) for the new generation of jet fighters designated Eurofighter 2000.

The ministry, responding to repeated speculation about the price in the German media, said each plane would cost 125.4 million marks, a reduction of 28 percent against original proposals from the four-nation consortium building the plane.
"The total costs are just about 23 billion marks," the ministry said in a statement. The industry consortium initially requested 26 billion marks for 180 planes from the German government.
"This is the result of long and hard negotiations between Defense Minister Volker Ruehe and industry in which the price could be drastically cut by 28 percent," the ministry added.
Germany has ordered 180 aircraft from the industry consortium which is made up of Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG of Germany, British Aerospace, Alenia of Italy and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA of Spain.

The ministry dismissed criticism from the main opposition Social Democrats, who said the government did not know what it buying. It said the order included the aircraft, logistical equipment, training simulators and miscellaneous accessories for the weapons system. ($1=1.6040 Mark)
